To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GPS point features can be integrated into LRMs, and vice versa; however, the integration is complicated and may require the use of a spatial database.

GPS point data can be integrated with linear referencing methods (1) if the GPS data are accurate and precise enough and (2) if they are collected in a manner that is compatible with the LRM and the data are processed in a manner that takes into account the inherent differences in GPS and LRS data.
GPS and LRM data can be integrated if the data are collected with a common reference frame (i.e., the same datum and projection).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of GPS point data into LRM systems.
the integration of spatial point features with linear referencing methods.
the issues of integrating spatial data collected with a GPS into a typical LRM and between LRMs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GPS data can be successfully integrated with an LRM, but the process is complicated by many variables.
the integration of GPS data into an LRM is possible, but the process is complex and requires the development of a detailed integration plan.
the integration of GPS data and LRMs is not a trivial task and that the integration is not a one-time process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GPS data can be successfully integrated with LRSs, but the process is not straightforward.
GPS is not a panacea for all spatial-data-collection problems and that GPS data should be used with caution when integrating with LRS data.

GPS data should be integrated with LRM data, but that it is important to recognize and address the issues that arise from integrating these two fundamentally different data-collection and data-management systems.

the integration of spatial data with LRM is not trivial and requires careful consideration.
GPS data must be integrated into the LRM or LRMs to be useful, and the integration process can be difficult and error prone.
